subject: MSA & Order Form: Term / Renewal — proposed compromise and next steps
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@veridianlabs.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: legal@veridianlabs.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA & Order Form — term / renewal redlines

Logan —

Thanks for the redlines earlier. Attached are Veridian's counter-redlines to the MSA and the Order Form; the two items we need clarity on are the auto-renew mechanics and the termination-for-convenience (TFC) language. High level:

- Auto-renew: we want the Order Form to auto-renew for successive 12-month terms unless either party gives 90 days' notice prior to renewal. That provides continuity for our internal planning.
- Notice window: we proposed 90 days above; we understand engineering ramp costs, so open to negotiating a phased notice (e.g., 90-day notice for auto-renew, 30-day operational notice for capacity reductions).
- Termination for convenience: we asked for a right to terminate Order Forms with 60 days' notice but proposed a termination fee equal to 25% of remaining committed TCV for the remainder of the then-current year.

Can Redwood confirm whether the platform can commit to: 1) preserving existing provisioned capacity for a 60-day wind-down after a termination notice, and 2) providing prorated credits for prepaid months if the TFC is exercised? Those are important for our finance team.

Attachments: Veridian_MSA_redline_v2.pdf (redlines), OrderForm_Veridian_lineitems.xlsx

Alex
Head of Procurement
Veridian Labs

--
On further detail: we flagged a couple of clauses around notice delivery (email vs. registered mail) and change of control carve-outs. If you want, we can jump on a 30-minute call later today to walk through the PDFs.
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MSA & Order Form — term / renewal redlines

Marissa / Rishi —

Forwarding Veridian's redlines (attached). Key asks call out: 90d auto-renew notice; 60d TFC with 25% remaining-commit fee; operational preservation of capacity for a 60d wind-down; and a preference for registered-delivery on notices.

My take: we should avoid hard 90d auto-renew for all customers — that's a customer risk to lock into (sales implications) — but we can accept a mutual 90d notice for enterprise-sized committed deals with an explicit carve-out that trials/pilots are month-to-month. Proposed compromise to present to Veridian:

1) Auto-renew: mutual renew for successive 12-month terms unless either party provides at least 60 days' prior written notice (compromise between 90d and our standard 30d). For Strategic/Enterprise deals (TCV > $1M), either party may request a 90d notice period that must be reflected on the Order Form.

2) Notice mechanics: Notices can be delivered by email to contract@redwoodinference.com or by registered mail; explicit mailbox addresses are included in the MSA.

3) Termination for convenience: allow TFC with 60 days' notice, limited to Order Form level (not MSA), with termination fee tiers — 0% after 12 months, 25% of remaining annualized TCV if terminated within first 12 months, and prorated credits for any prepaid months. We should say Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to maintain capacity for 60 days after notice but cannot guarantee burst capacity beyond committed pool.

Rishi — can you draft redline language that follows the above and include an explicit exception that preserves the KV cache and KV-transfer window for 30 days post-notice? Also make sure the billing/proration language ties to our invoicing cadence.

Marissa — can you confirm whether Sales is comfortable with a clear 'enterprise exception' for the 90d ask? If not, we'll push 60d as the default and leave an Order Form checkbox for 90d.

I'll propose a short call with Alex mid-day tomorrow if legal provides a clean redline by EOD.

Thanks,
Logan
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Logan / Rishi —

Thanks — quick notes inline. Draft redline snippet below for the TFC and auto-renew compromise. Please review and flag any billing pitfalls.

--- Proposed snippet (to be inserted into Section 4 / Order Form):
"""
Auto-Renewal. Unless otherwise specified on the applicable Order Form, each Order Form will automatically renew for successive twelve (12) month periods unless either party gives the other written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current Term. For Order Forms with a total contract value equal to or greater than USD $1,000,000, the parties may elect on the Order Form to require a ninety (90) day notice period in lieu of the sixty (60) day period above.

Termination for Convenience. Either party may terminate an Order Form for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice. If Customer terminates an Order Form for convenience within the first twelve (12) months following the Order Form Effective Date, Customer will pay a termination fee equal to twenty-five percent (25%) of the remaining committed TCV for the then-current twelve (12) month period; after twelve (12) months this fee does not apply. Any prepaid but unused fees shall be prorated and credited in accordance with Redwood's standard billing practices. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to preserve capacity for a sixty (60) day wind-down period following notice and to provide reasonable assistance to export Customer data and KV cache contents within thirty (30) days of termination.
"""

Two asks for Rishi: 1) ensure language around "commercially reasonable efforts" doesn't create a hard SLA exposure (we can say "no SLA"), and 2) include a short sentence that explicitly disclaims liability for third-party cloud costs incurred by the customer post-termination.

If you both sign off, I'll send this back to Alex with a cover note proposing a call Wednesday 10am PT.

Marissa
Senior Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Alex —

Thanks for sending through the PDFs. We've gone through the redlines internally and propose the following compromise, which we believe balances Veridian's need for planning visibility and Redwood's need to preserve standard product economics:

- Auto-renew: Default 60 days' written notice prior to renewal; Order Forms >= $1M can opt into a 90-day notice on the Order Form.
- Notice mechanics: email to contract@redwoodinference.com is acceptable; registered mail remains an option.
- Termination for convenience: allowed at Order Form level with 60 days' written notice. If exercised within the first 12 months, a termination fee equal to 25% of the remaining committed TCV for the then-current 12-month period applies. After 12 months, no termination fee. Prepaid amounts will be prorated and credited per Redwood billing policy. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts (no SLA) to maintain capacity for a 60-day wind-down and to provide export assistance for up to 30 days following termination.

I've attached a redline that inserts the Marissa/Rishi language into the MSA and call-out for an Order Form checkbox to elect 90d for enterprise deals. Please review and let us know whether this is acceptable. If so, I'll circulate a DocuSign package for the amended Order Form and MSA addendum.

Call options: Wed 16 Jul, 10:00am PT or Thu 17 Jul, 9:00am PT — happy to take the 30-minute slot.
